sections.markdown:
## C — Who needs a Missouri license, permit and license classes, required documents, fees and restriction codes
Knowledge domain: who must hold a Missouri driver license and who is exempt, the permit and license classes with their starting ages, which applicants take the full examination, the lawful status, identity, residency and Social Security proofs, the fee chart, and the restriction and medical-referral rules.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
Driving a motor vehicle or a motor-driven cycle on Missouri public roads requires a valid driver license, which any Missouri license office can issue. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
A Missouri resident who is at least 16 years old and plans to drive needs a Missouri license, and so does a new resident who wants to drive, even while holding another state's license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
An out-of-state commercial driver who moved to Missouri within the last 30 days must obtain a Missouri license, as explained in the separate commercial manual. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
Members of the armed forces and full-time students who hold a valid license from their home state do not need a Missouri license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
You must carry your license or permit whenever you drive, show it when a law enforcement officer asks, and never let another person use it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
The instruction permit, available at age 15, is the first step of the Graduated Driver License (GDL) program and lets a young person learn while supervised by a licensed adult. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
The driver examination record from the Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP) is not a permit or license; you bring it and your documents to a license office to be issued the actual credential. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
The six-month permit period needed before an intermediate license only begins once the temporary instruction permit has been issued. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle instruction permit at age 15 and a half (15 years and 182 days) requires a completed approved rider training course, passing the Class F and Class M written, vision and road sign tests, and written parent or guardian consent. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A02
The age 15 and a half motorcycle permit allows daylight riding only, within 50 miles of home, on a motorcycle of 250 cc or less, with no passengers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A02
From age 16 the rider training course is not required for a motorcycle instruction permit, but an applicant without a valid driver license must still take the Class F and Class M written tests. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A02
The intermediate license (Class F), available at 16, is the second GDL step and gives a young driver restricted privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
The full Class F license, available at 18, is the basic operator license and is required for any motor vehicle that does not call for a Class A, B, C or E license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
A Class F license does not cover motorcycles unless it shows the M endorsement, and getting one requires passing the Class F written, vision, road sign and driving tests. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
The Class E for-hire license, available at 18, has a written exam drawn from the whole guide but mostly Chapter 15, plus vision and road sign tests; a current Class F holder skips the driving test, and an 18-year-old must still meet the under-21 requirements. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
Class E applies when you are paid to drive a vehicle carrying 14 or fewer passengers, or you haul property for pay or as part of your job. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
Class E also applies when your job has you regularly drive someone else's freight vehicle rated 26,000 pounds GVWR or less that needs no hazardous-materials placard. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A03
Class E is not required for eligible ride-share (Transportation Network Company) or taxi drivers using vehicles of 12,000 pounds gross weight or less, or for prepared-food delivery drivers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A03
A Class M license, available at 16, or a license with the M endorsement is needed to ride a motorcycle or motortricycle on public roads, and GDL rules apply to Class M applicants aged 16 to 18. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A03
A commercial driver license requires age 18, and a CDL with a Hazardous Materials or School Bus endorsement requires age 21. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A03
A nondriver ID expires on your birthday in the sixth year after you apply, and applicants aged 70 or older get a non-expiring card, though a REAL ID applicant of that age may get a six-year card and immigration document review can shorten the term. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A03
Drivers aged 15 to 21 fall under the GDL program and must prove lawful status, identity with full legal name and date of birth, Social Security number, any name change, and Missouri residency. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A04
A new Missouri license requires the four-part examination: a written test, a vision test, a road sign test and a driving skills test. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A04
A new resident transferring an out-of-state license surrenders that license, takes only the vision and road sign tests, and every license, permit or ID from the other state becomes invalid. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A04
The four-part exam is also required when a Missouri license or an out-of-state license has been expired more than 184 days, after a revocation for too many points or an Administrative Alcohol Revocation, or when the Director of Revenue asks you to take it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A04
A U.S. citizen proves lawful status with a certified birth certificate bearing a vital records seal, a valid U.S. passport, or a certificate of citizenship, naturalization or birth abroad; hospital certificates and birth registration cards are refused. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A04
A vital-records copy of a birth certificate paired with a military ID card or discharge papers proves lawful status for a standard card but not for a REAL ID-compliant one. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A05
Missouri residency can be shown with items such as two current utility bills, a property tax receipt, a voter ID card, or an official government letter on letterhead dated within the last 90 days. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A05
A REAL ID-compliant card needs two residency documents, a non-REAL ID card needs one, and a separate mailing address needs its own proof. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A05
A post office box cannot serve as a residential address, and the license is mailed to the address you give. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A05
An applicant under 21 without an acceptable address document may use one supplied by a parent or legal guardian, but for REAL ID it counts as only one of the two residency proofs. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A05
State law requires your Social Security number on the application, proven by an original signed unlaminated card, a W-2, a 1099, or a paystub showing your name and number. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A06
Permit and license fees and how long the credential lasts depend on the applicant's age on the day of the transaction. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A06
The fee chart lists the intermediate license at minimum age 16 for $14.00, valid up to 2 years. [A06]
Why it matters: dynamic detail: fees can change; confirm on the Department of Revenue website.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A06
The fee chart lists the full Class F license at minimum age 18 for $16.50 for up to 3 years or $33.00 for up to 6 years. [A06]
Why it matters: dynamic detail: fees can change.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A06
The fee chart lists the instruction permit at age 15 for $10.00, valid up to 12 months, and the student permit at 15 for $1.00 for the length of the approved course. [A06]
Why it matters: dynamic detail: fees can change.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A07
A driver with limited experience or a medical condition affecting safe driving may get a restricted license, and removing a restriction can require a driving test. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A07
Ignoring a restriction can bring a charge of driving without a license and, on conviction, points on your record. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A07
Among the restriction codes, A means corrective lenses, C daylight driving only, F a limit of 45 MPH, G a 25 mile radius and I the intermediate license. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A07
A physician's statement can be required if you had epileptic seizures, convulsions or blackouts in the six months before applying. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F41 | anchor: A07
Endorsements work opposite to restrictions: they add privileges such as driving a school bus or a motorcycle to a Class F, E or M license. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0011]

Misconceptions: the Highway Patrol test record is not a permit; a full-time student or service member with a home-state license is exempt, but a new resident is not; transferring an out-of-state license still means the vision and road sign tests; a post office box is never a residential address.
Mnemonics: permit, intermediate, full is the GDL ladder; Class F is the family car, Class E is earning money behind the wheel, Class M is motorcycle.
Glossary: GDL means the Graduated Driver License program; Class F is the operator license; Class E is the for-hire license; endorsement means an added privilege; restriction code means a letter limiting how or when you may drive; REAL ID-compliant means the federally accepted card version with stricter documents.
Dynamic facts: the license and permit fees in the chart, website document lists and office contact details can change and must be refreshed from the Department of Revenue website.
